When Jesus heard the news, he got into a boat and went off to a deserted place to be alone. But the crowds found out, and they came after him on foot from the towns. As he stepped ashore, he saw a large crowd. He felt deep pity for them, and he healed those among them who were sick. When evening came, the disciples went to him and said, “There is nothing out here, and the day is nearly over. Let the crowds go now, so they can find food to buy in the villages.” But Jesus told them, “They do not have to go away. Give them food yourselves.” They said to him, “We have nothing here but five loaves and two fish.” He told them, “Bring them over here to me.” He had the people sit down on the grass. Then he took the five loaves and the two fish, raised his eyes to heaven, and spoke the blessing. He broke the loaves and handed them to the disciples, and the disciples passed them to the crowds. Everyone ate and had enough. Then they collected what remained of the broken pieces, and it filled twelve baskets. The men who ate numbered about 5,000, not counting women and children.

Jesus comes to them across the water

Straight after this, Jesus insisted that the disciples get into the boat and go on before him across the lake. Meanwhile he would send the crowds home. Once the crowds had gone, he climbed up into the hills by himself to pray. Evening came, and he was still there by himself. By then the boat was a mile or more from shore, and the waves were pounding it, since the wind was blowing against them. In the last watch of the night, he came out to them, walking on the water. The disciples saw him coming across the water and were thrown into panic. “A ghost!” they cried, and they shouted out in terror. Jesus spoke to them at once: “Be brave! It is I. There is nothing to fear.”

Peter answered him, “Lord, if it is really you, give me the order to come to you over the water.” “Come,” he said. So Peter climbed down out of the boat, stepped onto the water, and walked toward Jesus. But when he noticed how strong the wind was, fear took hold of him. He started to go under, and he shouted, “Lord, save me!” Jesus at once put out his hand and took hold of him. “You have so little faith,” he said to him. “Why did you doubt?” As soon as the two of them had climbed into the boat, the wind dropped. Everyone in the boat fell down and worshiped him. “You really are the Son of God!” they said.

Healing at Gennesaret

After crossing the lake, they came ashore at Gennesaret. The people of that place knew who he was, and they sent messengers all through the region around. They brought to him everyone who was ill and pleaded to be allowed simply to touch the tassel of his cloak. Every one of them who touched it was fully healed.
fields.summary: Herod has John the Baptist beheaded. Jesus feeds a great crowd with five loaves and two fish, comes to the disciples across the water, where Peter starts to sink, and heals the sick at Gennesaret.

fields.title: Matthew 15
fields.body_html:
The elders’ tradition and God’s command

Then Pharisees and scribes arrived from Jerusalem and put a question to Jesus: “Why do your disciples go against the tradition handed down by the elders? They eat their meals without first washing their hands.” He answered them, “And why do you go against God’s commandment for the sake of your tradition? For God said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and also, ‘Anyone who reviles father or mother must be put to death.’ But you teach that if someone says to father or mother, ‘Any support you could have received from me is set apart as a gift to God,’ then that person is excused from honoring their father. So for the sake of your tradition you have cancelled God’s word. You are hypocrites, and Isaiah’s prophecy about you was exactly right. He said: ‘With their lips this people honors me, but their heart keeps far away from me. Their worship of me is empty, for the doctrines they teach are commands made by human beings.’”

What makes a person unclean

Then Jesus called the crowd over to him and said, “Hear this, and understand it. A person is not made unclean by what goes into the mouth. What makes a person unclean is what comes out of it.”

Then the disciples came to him and said, “Are you aware that the Pharisees took offense at what you said?” He answered, “Any plant that my Father in heaven did not plant will be torn out, roots and all. Pay no attention to them. They are blind, yet they guide others who are blind. When one blind person guides another, the two of them end up in a ditch.”

Peter spoke up: “Tell us what this parable means.” He said, “Are even you still so slow to understand? Can you not see that everything taken in by the mouth goes down into the stomach and is then passed out into the latrine? But what comes out of the mouth has its source in the heart, and that is what makes a person unclean. It is from the heart that evil schemes come, and murder, adultery and other sexual sin, theft, false witness and abusive speech. These are what make a person unclean. Eating without washing one’s hands does not make anyone unclean.”

A Canaanite mother’s faith

Jesus left that place and went away to the region around Tyre and Sidon. A Canaanite woman who lived in that region came out and kept calling out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! A demon has my daughter in its grip, and she suffers terribly.” But he gave her no answer, not even a word. His disciples came and kept pressing him: “Send her away, because she keeps shouting behind us.” He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep, the people of Israel.” But she came and bowed low before him. “Lord,” she said, “help me!” He replied, “It is not good to take bread away from the children and toss it to the little dogs.” She said, “That is true, Lord. Still, the little dogs eat some of the crumbs that drop from the table where their masters eat.” Then Jesus told her, “Woman, your faith is great. May it be done for you as you wish.” And from that moment her daughter was well.

Healing on the mountain by the lake

From there Jesus moved on and came along the shore of the Sea of Galilee. He went up onto the mountain and sat down there. Large crowds came to him, bringing people who could not speak, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others. They laid them down at his feet, and he healed them. The crowd was amazed to see the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking and the blind able to see. And they glorified the God of Israel.

Bread for four thousand

Jesus called his disciples together and said, “I feel deep pity for the crowd. For three days now they have stayed with me, and they have nothing left to eat. If I send them off without food, they may give out on the way, and I am not willing to do that.” The disciples said to him, “Here in this lonely place, where could we find enough bread to feed such a crowd?” Jesus asked them, “How many loaves have you got?” “Seven,” they said, “and a few little fish.” He told the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then he took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and broke them. He kept handing them to the disciples, and the disciples handed them to the people. Everyone ate until they were full. Then they gathered up the leftover pieces, and these filled seven large baskets. Those who ate numbered 4,000 men, and there were women and children besides. After sending the crowds away, he got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.
fields.summary: Jesus tells the Pharisees and scribes that their tradition sets aside God’s command and that what makes a person unclean comes from the heart. A Canaanite mother’s faith wins healing for her daughter, and Jesus heals many by the lake and feeds four thousand.

fields.title: Matthew 16
fields.body_html:
Asked for a sign from heaven

Pharisees and Sadducees came to put Jesus to the test. They asked him to show them a sign from heaven. He answered them, “In the evening you say, ‘It will be fine weather, because the sky is red.’ And in the morning you say, ‘There will be a storm today, because the sky is red and threatening.’ You know how to read the face of the sky, but you cannot read the signs of the times.

An evil, unfaithful generation goes looking for a sign, but the only sign it will be given is the sign of Jonah.” Then he left them and went away.

Watch out for their yeast

When the disciples reached the other side of the lake, they found that they had forgotten to bring any bread. Jesus told them, “Keep your eyes open, and guard yourselves against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” They talked it over among themselves and said, “He says that because we brought no bread.” Jesus knew what they were saying, and he said, “Why are you talking among yourselves about having no bread, you who have so little faith? Do you still not understand? Have you forgotten the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered? Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many large basketfuls you gathered? How can you fail to see that I was not talking to you about bread? Guard yourselves, I say, against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” Then they realized that he was not warning them against the yeast used in bread, but against what the Pharisees and Sadducees taught.

Peter’s answer at Caesarea Philippi

When Jesus reached the district around Caesarea Philippi, he put a question to his disciples: “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?” They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; still others, Jeremiah or another of the prophets.” Then he asked them, “And you, who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus said to him in reply, “You are blessed, Simon son of Jonah! No human being showed you this; it was my Father in heaven. And I tell you: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church. The gates of the realm of the dead will not overpower it. I will hand you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: what you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and what you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.” Then he gave the disciples strict orders not to tell anyone that he was the Christ.

Jesus speaks of his coming death

From then on Jesus began to show his disciples plainly that he must go to Jerusalem. There he would suffer much from the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes; he would be killed, and on the third day he would be raised. Peter drew him aside and began to object. “God forbid it, Lord!” he said. “Nothing like this will ever happen to you!” Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block in my way. Your mind is not on God’s purposes but on human ones.”

Taking up the cross

Then Jesus told his disciples, “Anyone who wishes to come after me must say no to self, pick up their cross, and follow me. Those who want to secure their own life will lose it, and those who lose their life for my sake will find it. Suppose someone gains the whole world but forfeits their life. What good will that do them? Or what could anyone give to buy back their life? For the Son of Man is going to come with his angels in the glory of his Father, and then he will repay each person for what they have done. Truly I tell you, among those standing here are some who will not taste death until they have seen the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.”
fields.summary: Jesus refuses the leaders a sign and warns against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees. At Caesarea Philippi Peter declares who Jesus is, and Jesus begins to speak of suffering, death and rising, and of taking up the cross.

fields.title: Matthew 17
fields.body_html:
Jesus transfigured on the mountain

Six days later Jesus took Peter and James and James’s brother John with him and led them up a high mountain, where they were alone. There, before their eyes, he was transfigured. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes turned white as light. Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus. Peter spoke up and said to Jesus, “Lord, how good it is that we are here! If you want, I will put up three shelters here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” Peter was still speaking when a cloud full of light covered them with its shadow, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is my dearly loved Son, and I delight in him. Listen to him.” Hearing the voice, the disciples fell face down on the ground in great fear. Then Jesus came over, laid his hand on them, and said, “Get up, and stop being afraid.” When they raised their eyes, they saw no one there but Jesus alone.

Elijah has already come

On the way down the mountain Jesus gave them this order: “Tell no one about the vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.” So the disciples questioned him: “If that is so, why do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?” He answered, “Elijah is indeed coming, and he will set all things right. But I tell you that Elijah has come already. They did not recognize him, and they treated him however they pleased. They will make the Son of Man suffer in the same way.” The disciples then realized that he meant John the Baptist.

A boy with seizures is healed

When they reached the crowd, a man came up to him and knelt in front of him. “Lord,” he said, “take pity on my son. He has seizures and suffers terribly. Time and again he falls into the fire, and time and again into the water. I brought him to your disciples, but they did not have the power to heal him.” Jesus replied, “You faithless and twisted generation! How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy over here to me.” Jesus spoke sternly to the demon, and it came out of the boy. From that moment he was well.

Then, when they were alone with Jesus, the disciples asked him, “What kept us from driving it out?” He told them, “It is because your faith is so small. Truly I tell you, if you have faith even the size of a mustard seed, you can tell this mountain, ‘Go from here to over there,’ and it will go. There will be nothing you cannot do.”

Jesus speaks again of his death and raising

As they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is going to be given over into the power of human beings. They will put him to death, and on the third day he will be raised up.” And the disciples were filled with deep sorrow.

The tax for God’s house

When they arrived in Capernaum, the men who collected the temple tax came to Peter and said, “Your teacher pays the temple tax, does he not?” “Yes, he does,” Peter answered. When Peter came into the house, Jesus spoke to him before he could say anything. “Simon,” he said, “tell me what you think. When the kings of the earth take tolls or taxes, who pays them? From their own sons, or from people outside their family?” “From outsiders,” Peter replied. Jesus said to him, “So the sons owe nothing. Still, we do not want to give them a reason to take offense. So go down to the lake and throw in a hook. Take the first fish that comes up, open its mouth, and you will find a silver coin worth four days’ wages. Take it and give it to them for me and for you.”
fields.summary: Jesus is transfigured on the mountain and explains that Elijah has already come. Jesus heals a boy with seizures, speaks again of death and raising, and provides the tax for God’s house from the mouth of a fish.

fields.title: Matthew 18
fields.body_html:
Who is greatest in the kingdom

Just then the disciples came to Jesus with a question: “So who ranks highest in the kingdom of heaven?” He called a little child over and stood the child among them. Then he said, “Truly I tell you, if you do not turn around and become like children, you will not get into the kingdom of heaven at all. So the greatest in the kingdom of heaven is anyone who takes a low place, as this child does. And when someone welcomes a child like this for my sake, it is me they welcome.

Woe to those who trip up the little ones

But if anyone leads into sin one of these little ones who believe in me, that person would be better off sunk far out at sea with a great millstone fastened around their neck. Woe to the world for the snares that trip people into sin! Such snares are sure to come, but woe to anyone who brings one about!

If your hand or your foot leads you into sin, cut it off and get rid of it. You are better off entering life maimed or lame than keeping both hands or both feet and being thrown into the eternal fire. And if your eye leads you into sin, pull it out and get rid of it. You are better off entering life with one eye than keeping both eyes and being thrown into the fire of hell.

The Father seeks the sheep that strays

Take care never to look down on a single one of these little ones. I tell you, their angels in heaven stand always in the presence of my Father in heaven. Tell me what you think. Suppose someone owns a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders off. Will the owner not leave the ninety-nine on the hillsides and set out to search for the one that strayed? And if the owner does find it, truly I tell you, that one sheep brings more delight than the ninety-nine that never wandered off. So too, your Father in heaven does not wish to lose even one of these little ones.

When a fellow believer sins against you

If a brother or sister sins against you, go and confront them about it, with only the two of you present. If they will listen to you, you have won your brother or sister back. If they still will not listen, go back with one or two others, so that ‘every charge may be settled on the word of two or three witnesses.’ If they will not hear them either, bring the matter before the church. And if they will not hear the church either, regard them as an outsider, like a Gentile or a tax collector. Truly I tell you, what you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and what you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

And again, truly I tell you: if two of you here on earth are of one mind about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven. For whenever two or three come together in my name, I am there among them.”

How many times to forgive

Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, if a brother or sister keeps on sinning against me, how many times must I forgive? As many as seven times?” Jesus told him, “Not just up to seven times, but up to seventy-seven times.

The servant who would not forgive

That is why the kingdom of heaven is like this: a king decided it was time to go over the accounts of his servants. As he began, a man was brought before him who owed him a sum no worker could earn in a hundred thousand years. He had no means of paying, so his master gave orders for him to be sold, together with his wife, his children and all he owned, to pay toward the debt. At that the servant threw himself to the ground before him and pleaded, ‘Give me time, and I will pay back all of it.’ The master was moved with pity for that servant. He set him free and forgave him the debt. But no sooner had that servant left than he came upon one of his fellow servants who owed him about a hundred days’ wages. He grabbed him by the throat. ‘Pay me what you owe!’ he said. His fellow servant dropped to the ground and pleaded with him, ‘Give me time, and I will pay you back.’ But he would not hear of it. He went off and had the man put in prison until the debt was paid. When the other servants saw what had taken place, they were deeply upset. They went to their master and told him the whole story. So the master had him called back and said to him, ‘Wicked servant! You pleaded with me, and I forgave you the whole of that debt. Should you not have shown your fellow servant the same mercy I showed you?’ Then the master, now angry, gave him over to the torturers, to stay with them until he had repaid the whole debt.

My Father in heaven will deal with you in the same way if you do not forgive your brother or sister from the heart, each one of you.”
fields.summary: Jesus teaches that the greatest in the kingdom is the one who becomes like a child, warns against tripping up the little ones and tells of the Father seeking a sheep that strays. Jesus teaches how to deal with a fellow believer’s sin and to forgive without limit, telling of a servant who would not forgive.

fields.title: Matthew 19
fields.body_html:
Jesus leaves Galilee for Judea

When Jesus had finished saying these things, he left Galilee and went on into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan. Great crowds went after him, and there he healed them.

A question about divorce

Some Pharisees came to him to put him to the test. “Does the law allow a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?” they asked. Jesus answered, “Have you never read that the Creator, at the beginning, made them male and female? And he said, ‘That is why a man will leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh.’ So they are not two any longer; they are one flesh. What God has yoked together, then, no human being may pull apart.” They said to him, “Then why did Moses order a man to give his wife a written notice of divorce and send her away?” Jesus answered, “It was because your hearts were so hard that Moses permitted you to divorce your wives. That is not how things were at the beginning. And I tell you this: a man who divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual unfaithfulness and then marries someone else commits adultery, and the man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”

Those who do not marry

His disciples said to him, “If that is how it stands between a man and his wife, then it would be better not to marry at all.” He answered them, “This saying is not something everyone can accept. Only those to whom it has been given can do so. For some are eunuchs because they were born that way; some have been made eunuchs by others; and some have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let anyone who is able to accept this accept it.”

Jesus blesses the children

After this, some people brought young children to Jesus so that he would put his hands on them and pray for them. But the disciples spoke sternly to the people. Jesus said, “Let the children be. Do not prevent them from coming to me, because the kingdom of heaven is for those who are like them.” He put his hands on them, and then he went on from there.

A young man asks about eternal life

Then a man came up to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to gain eternal life?” Jesus answered him, “Why ask me about what is good? There is one who is good. If you wish to enter into life, obey the commandments.” “Which ones?” the man asked. Jesus said, “‘Do not commit murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not give false testimony; honor your father and your mother’; and ‘love your neighbor as yourself.’” The young man said to him, “I have obeyed every one of these. What am I still missing?” Jesus told him, “Do you want to be perfect? Then go, sell your property, and give the money to people who are poor, and treasure in heaven will be yours. After that, come and follow me.” When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he owned a great deal of property.

Hard for the rich

Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Truly I tell you, a rich person will find it hard to get into the kingdom of heaven. I say it again: a camel could pass through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could enter the kingdom of God.” The disciples were utterly amazed at this. “Then who can be saved?” they asked. Jesus looked straight at them and said, “For human beings this cannot be done, but for God everything is possible.”

What the Twelve will receive

Then Peter spoke up. “We have left everything behind and followed you,” he said to him. “So what will we receive?” Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, when all things are made new and the Son of Man takes his seat on his glorious throne, you who have followed me will also take your seats on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel. Anyone who has left behind houses, or brothers or sisters, or father or mother, or wife or children, or fields, for the sake of my name will be repaid a hundred times over and will receive eternal life as an inheritance. But many who are first now will end up last, and the last will end up first.
fields.summary: In Judea Jesus answers a question about divorce, blesses the children and tells a young man who asks about eternal life to sell what he has. It is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom, but the Twelve will receive a great reward.

fields.title: Matthew 20
fields.body_html:
Workers hired at every hour

For this is what the kingdom of heaven is like: a landowner went out at first light to hire laborers to work in his vineyard. He settled with the laborers on the usual wage for a day and sent them off into his vineyard. Around nine in the morning he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace with nothing to do. ‘You too, go to the vineyard,’ he told them, ‘and I will give you what is fair.’ So they went. He went out again around noon, and again around three in the afternoon, and did the same. Then, about five in the afternoon, he went out and found still others standing there. ‘Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?’ he asked them. ‘Because nobody has hired us,’ they answered. He told them, ‘You go to the vineyard too.’ When evening came, the owner of the vineyard told his manager, ‘Call in the laborers and give them their pay. Start with the ones hired last and finish with the first.’ Those hired around five o’clock came, and each of them was given a full day’s wage. So when the first ones came, they expected to get more. But they too were each paid a day’s wage. When they were paid, they began to grumble at the landowner. ‘The ones who came last put in a single hour,’ they said, ‘and you have treated them the same as us, though we carried the load of the whole day in the burning heat.’ But he replied to one of them, ‘Friend, I have done you no wrong. Was it not for a day’s wage that you made your agreement with me? Take what is yours and be on your way. It is my choice to give this last worker just what I gave you. Do I not have the right to do as I please with what belongs to me? Or do you look on my generosity with an evil eye?’ That is how it will be: those who are last will be first, and those who are first, last.”

A third warning of death and rising

As Jesus was on his way up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, away from the others, and spoke to them as they walked. “We are going up to Jerusalem now. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will sentence him to death and turn him over to the Gentiles, who will mock him, whip him, and crucify him. And on the third day he will be raised to life.”

A mother’s request for her sons

Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came up to him together with her sons. She knelt in front of him and asked him for a favor. “What is it you want?” he asked her. She said to him, “Give your word that in your kingdom these two sons of mine will sit beside you, one at your right and one at your left.” Jesus answered, “You do not realize what you are asking. The cup I am about to drink: are you able to drink it?” “We are able,” they answered. He told them, “You will indeed drink my cup. But the places at my right and left are not mine to hand out. They belong to those for whom my Father has prepared them.”

Great ones and servants

The other ten were furious with the two brothers when they heard of this. Jesus called them together and said, “You know that among the Gentiles, rulers act as lords over their people, and the powerful wield their authority over them. With you it must be different. If any of you wants to become great, that one must serve the rest of you. And if any of you wants to be first, that one must be your slave. It is the same with the Son of Man. He did not come so that others would wait on him. He came to serve them, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

Two blind men by the Jericho road

A large crowd went along behind him as he and the disciples left Jericho. Beside the road sat two blind men. They heard that Jesus was passing, and they began to shout, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!” The crowd scolded them and told them to keep quiet, but they only shouted louder, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!” Jesus stood still and called to them. “What would you like me to do for you?” he asked. “Lord,” they replied, “we want our eyes to be opened.” Jesus felt deep pity for them and touched their eyes. At once they could see, and they followed him.
fields.summary: Jesus tells of workers hired at every hour and paid the same, and warns a third time of death and rising. When a mother asks for places of honor for her sons, Jesus says the great must be servants, and two blind men near Jericho receive their sight.

fields.title: Matthew 21
fields.body_html:
The king comes to Jerusalem on a donkey

When they were getting close to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples on ahead with instructions: “Go into the village across from you, and straightaway you will come upon a donkey tied up there with her colt. Untie them and lead them to me. If anyone questions you, say, ‘The Lord needs them.’ Then he will let them go at once.”

This happened so that the word spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled: “Tell the daughter of Zion, ‘Your king is coming to you! He is gentle, and he is seated on a donkey and on a colt, the foal of a pack animal.’” The disciples went off and did what Jesus had told them. They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and he sat on them. The crowd, which was very large, spread their own cloaks across the road, and others kept cutting branches from the trees and laying them on the road. Crowds walked in front of him and behind him, and they kept shouting, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heavens!” When he came into Jerusalem, the whole city was in an uproar. “Who is this man?” people asked. And the crowds kept saying, “This is the prophet, Jesus, the man from Nazareth in Galilee.”

Jesus clears the temple

Jesus went into the temple courts and drove out everyone who was buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the seats of the dove sellers. “It is written,” he told them, “‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are turning it into a hideout for robbers.”

Blind and lame people came to him in the temple courts, and he healed them. The chief priests and the scribes saw the amazing things he was doing, and they saw the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” They were furious, and they said to him, “Do you hear what these children are saying?” Jesus answered them, “I do. Did you never read this: ‘Out of the mouths of little children and nursing babies you have brought forth praise for yourself’?” Then he left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where he spent the night.

The fig tree with nothing but leaves

Early in the morning, as he was going back into the city, Jesus felt hungry. Seeing a fig tree beside the road, he went up to it, but he found nothing on it except leaves. Then he said to it, “From now on, may no fruit ever grow on you!” At once the fig tree dried up. The disciples were astonished when they saw this. “How did the fig tree dry up so quickly?” they asked. Jesus answered them, “Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will do more than what was done to this fig tree. Even if you tell this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will be done. And everything you ask for in prayer you will receive, as long as you believe.”

Who gave Jesus this authority?

Jesus went into the temple courts, and while he was teaching, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to him. “What authority do you have for doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave you this authority?” Jesus replied, “I too will put one question to you. If you answer it for me, then I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things. John’s baptism, where did it come from? Was it from heaven or from human beings?” They began to argue it out among themselves: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask us, ‘Then why did you not believe John?’ But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ we have the crowd to fear, since they all regard John as a prophet.” So they answered Jesus, “We do not know.” And he said to them, “Then I will not tell you either by what authority I do these things.

Two sons and their father’s will

Now tell me what you think. A man had two sons. He came to the first one and said, ‘Go and work in the vineyard today, son.’ He answered, ‘I do not want to.’ Yet afterward he changed his mind and went. Then the father went to the second son and said the same thing. This one answered, ‘I will, sir,’ but he did not go. Which of the two did what their father wanted?” “The first,” they answered. Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are leading the way into the kingdom of God, ahead of you. For John came to you showing the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and the prostitutes did believe him. And even after you saw that, you did not change your minds later and believe him.

The tenants who killed the owner’s son

Listen to another parable.

A man who owned an estate planted a vineyard. He set a hedge around it, cut a pit for a winepress, and put up a watchtower. Then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad. When harvest time came near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the crop. The tenants grabbed his servants. One they beat up, another they killed, and another they pelted with stones. So the owner sent other servants, a larger group than the first, and the tenants treated them the same way. Finally he sent his son to them. He told himself, ‘They will show respect to my son.’ The tenants, though, saw the son and said to one another, ‘Here is the one who will inherit the vineyard. Come on, if we kill him, his inheritance will be ours.’ They took hold of him, forced him outside the vineyard, and killed him. Now when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?” They answered him, “He will put those evil men to a miserable death, and he will lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will hand over the fruit to him at each harvest.”

Jesus said to them, “Did you never read this in the Scriptures: ‘The very stone the builders turned down has become the cornerstone. The Lord has brought this about, and we look on it with wonder’? This is why I tell you: you will lose the kingdom of God. It will be taken from you and given to a people that bears the fruit it calls for.

Whoever falls on this stone will be dashed to pieces, and if it falls on anyone, it will crush them to dust.”

The chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables and realized that he meant them. They wanted to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowds, who regarded him as a prophet.
fields.summary: Jesus comes into Jerusalem on a donkey, clears the temple and curses a fig tree with nothing but leaves. When the leaders question Jesus’s authority, Jesus answers with the parables of the two sons and of the tenants who killed the owner’s son.

fields.title: Matthew 22
fields.body_html:
The king’s wedding banquet

Once more Jesus answered them by speaking in parables: “What happens in the kingdom of heaven can be compared to this: a king prepared a wedding banquet for his son. He sent his servants to summon the guests who had already been invited, but they refused to come. So he sent more servants with this message: ‘Tell the guests, “See, my banquet is prepared. My bulls and my fattened calves have been slaughtered. Everything is ready, so come to the wedding.”‘ The guests did not care. They went off, one to his farm and another to his trade. The rest laid hands on the king’s servants, abused them, and killed them. The king was furious. He sent his troops, wiped out those murderers, and set their city on fire. Then he told his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but the guests I invited did not deserve to come. So go out to where the roads leave the city, and invite to the wedding anyone you come across.’ The servants went out into the streets and brought in everyone they could find, bad and good alike, and the wedding feast was crowded with guests. The king came in to look over his guests, and among them he saw a man who had not put on clothes for a wedding. He said to him, ‘Friend, how is it that you came in here with no wedding clothes on?’ The man had nothing to say. The king then gave orders to his attendants: ‘Bind his hands and feet and throw him out into the darkness outside, where people will weep and grind their teeth.’ For the invited are many, but the chosen are few.”

A question about paying Caesar

Then the Pharisees went off and plotted how they could catch Jesus out by his own words. They sent their own disciples to him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that you are truthful and that you teach God’s way in keeping with the truth. No one’s opinion moves you, for you do not judge people by their rank. So give us your opinion. Does the law permit paying the head tax to Caesar, or not?” Jesus was aware of their malice. “You hypocrites,” he said, “why are you putting me to the test? Show me the coin that pays the tax.” They brought him a silver coin worth a day’s wage. Then he asked them, “Whose portrait is this? And whose title is written on it?” “Caesar’s,” they answered. And he said to them, “Then pay Caesar what you owe Caesar, and pay God what you owe God.” His answer astonished them, and they went off and left him alone.

Marriage and the resurrection

That same day some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him with a question. “Teacher,” they said, “Moses gave this rule: ‘If a man dies and leaves no children, his brother is to take the widow as his wife and so give his dead brother descendants.’ There were seven brothers in our community. The first one married and died, and because he had no children, his widow went to his brother. The same thing happened to the second brother, and the third, and so on through all seven. Finally, after them all, the woman died. So when the dead are raised, which of the seven will have her as his wife? All of them were married to her.”

Jesus replied, “You have gone astray, because you understand neither the Scriptures nor God’s power. For once the dead are raised, men no longer take wives and women are no longer given as brides; they are like the angels of God in heaven. As for the dead being raised, have you not read what God said to you: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is God not of the dead but of the living.” His teaching amazed the crowds who heard it.

The command that ranks highest

The Pharisees heard that Jesus had put the Sadducees to silence, and they came together in one place. One of their number, a man trained in the law, put a question to him to test him: “Teacher, which commandment in the law ranks highest?” Jesus answered him, “‘Love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, and with your whole mind.’ This command is the great one, the first of all.

A second command is of the same kind: ‘Love your neighbor as you love yourself.’ The whole of the law, and the prophets as well, hangs on these two commands.”

Whose son is the Christ?

While the Pharisees were still gathered there, Jesus put a question to them: “What is your view of the Christ? Whose son is he?” “David’s,” they answered. He asked them, “Why then does David, moved by the Spirit, give him the title Lord? For David says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Take your seat at my right hand until I have put your enemies beneath your feet.”‘ So if David calls him ‘Lord’, how can he be David’s son?” None of them could give him any answer at all. And after that day no one was bold enough to put another question to him.
fields.summary: Jesus tells of a king’s wedding banquet and answers questions about paying Caesar, marriage at the resurrection and the command that ranks highest. Then Jesus asks the Pharisees how David’s son can also be David’s Lord, and no one can answer.

fields.title: Matthew 23
fields.body_html:
The teachers who sit in Moses’ seat

Then Jesus said to the crowds and to his disciples, “The scribes and the Pharisees have taken Moses’ seat. So practice and keep whatever they tell you. But do not follow their example, because they do not live by what they teach. They bundle up heavy loads and pile them on the shoulders of others, but they refuse to move those loads even with a finger. All their deeds are done for others to watch. They widen their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels. They are fond of the seat of honor at banquets and the front seats in the synagogues, of respectful greetings in the marketplaces, and of hearing people address them as ‘Rabbi.’ But as for you, do not let anyone call you ‘Rabbi.’ There is one who is your teacher, and all of you are brothers and sisters together. And do not give anyone on earth the title ‘father,’ because you have one Father, the one in heaven. Do not be called instructors either, because you have one instructor, the Christ. Whoever is greatest among you will be the one who serves you. Those who lift themselves up will be brought low, and those who make themselves low will be lifted up.

Woe to you, hypocrites

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You bar the way into the kingdom of heaven so that people cannot get in. You do not go in yourselves, and when others are on their way in, you stop them.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You journey across sea and land to win over one convert. Then, once you have done so, you turn that convert into someone twice as fit for hell as you are.

Woe to you, blind guides! This is what you teach: ‘Swearing by the temple counts for nothing. But swear by the gold of the temple, and you must keep your oath.’ Foolish and blind! Which is greater, then: the gold, or the temple that has set the gold apart as holy? You also teach: ‘Swearing by the altar counts for nothing. But swear by the gift lying on it, and you must keep your oath.’ How blind you are! Which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sets the gift apart as holy? So whoever swears by the altar is swearing by the altar and by all that lies on it. And whoever swears by the temple is swearing by the temple and by the one who dwells there. And whoever swears by heaven is swearing by God’s throne and by the one seated on it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You set aside for God a tenth even of your mint, dill and cumin, yet you have abandoned what weighs most in the law: justice, mercy and faithfulness. These are what you should have done, while still not abandoning the others. Blind guides! You sieve a gnat out of your drink and swallow a camel whole.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You wash the outside of cup and plate, but inside they are filled by robbery and self-indulgence. Blind Pharisee! Make the inside of cup and plate clean first, so that the outside becomes clean too.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You resemble tombs coated with whitewash. From outside they look fine, but within they are full of the bones of the dead and every kind of uncleanness. You are the same. To others you look righteous from the outside, but within you are full of hypocrisy and of disregard for God’s law.

The blood of the prophets

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You put up tombs for the prophets and adorn the memorials of the righteous. Then you declare, ‘If we had been alive when our ancestors were, we would never have joined them in killing the prophets.’ Your own words are evidence against you: you are the sons of the prophets’ murderers. Fill up, then, the measure of your ancestors’ sins! You snakes! You family of snakes! How can you flee from the sentence of hell? That is why I am sending you prophets, sages and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; others you will whip in your synagogues and hound from town to town. And so the guilt for all the innocent blood poured out on the earth will fall on you, from the blood of Abel, a righteous man, to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar. Truly I tell you, all these things will fall upon this generation. Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You murder the prophets and stone the messengers sent to you. How many times I have wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen draws her chicks under her wings! But you refused. Now your house is being abandoned to you, a desolate place. For I tell you, from now on you will not see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
fields.summary: Jesus warns the crowds and disciples about the scribes and Pharisees, who sit in Moses’ seat but do not practice what they teach. A series of woes against the hypocrites ends in a lament over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets.

fields.title: Matthew 24
fields.body_html:
Not one stone on another

As Jesus came out of the temple and went on his way, his disciples approached to point out its buildings to him. In answer he said to them, “You see all this, do you not? Truly I tell you, every stone here will be pulled down, until not one is left resting on another.”

The first birth pains

Later, while he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him by themselves and said, “Tell us when this will take place. And what sign will mark your coming and the close of the age?” Jesus replied, “Be on your guard, so that nobody leads you astray. Many will come and use my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray. You are going to hear of wars, and of news of wars. Take care not to be shaken. These things have to happen, but that does not mean the end has come. Nation will go to war with nation, and kingdom with kingdom. In one place after another there will be famines and earthquakes. Yet all of this is only the start of the birth pains.

Then they will hand you over for harsh treatment and kill you, and all the nations will hate you because of my name. Many will then fall away, handing each other over and hating each other. False prophets will rise up in great numbers, and they will lead many astray. As lawlessness spreads, most people’s love will cool. But whoever holds out to the end will be saved. This gospel of the kingdom will be announced throughout the world, so that every nation hears the witness, and only then will the end come.

Flee to the mountains

So when you see the abomination that brings ruin, of which the prophet Daniel spoke, standing in the holy place (let the reader take note), then those in Judea must escape to the hills. Anyone on the roof must not go down to fetch things from the house, and anyone in the field must not turn back for a cloak. Woe to women who are pregnant and to those nursing babies in those days! Pray that you will not have to escape in winter, or on a Sabbath day. For that will be a time of great distress, worse than anything that has happened since the world began, and nothing like it will ever happen again. Had those days not been cut short, not one person would come through alive. But for the sake of the chosen they will be cut short. If anyone says to you then, ‘Look, the Christ is here!’ or ‘He is here!’ refuse to believe it. People falsely claiming to be the Christ will rise up, and false prophets with them. They will work great signs and wonders, enough to lead astray even the chosen ones, if such a thing could be done. Mark this: I have warned you in advance. So if they tell you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ stay where you are. If they say, ‘Look, he is hidden indoors,’ do not believe it. The coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning that flashes in the east and lights up the sky all the way to the west. Where there is a dead body, that is where vultures flock.

The Son of Man on the clouds of heaven

Right after the distress of those days the sun will turn dark and the moon will stop giving its light. Stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Every tribe on earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on heaven’s clouds, with power and great glory. As a great trumpet sounds, he will send out his angels. They will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from the farthest edges of the heavens on every side.

Summer is near

Take the fig tree as your lesson. When its branches turn soft and leaves start to sprout, you can tell that summer is not far off. So it is with you: once you see all these things, be sure that it is close, standing at the door. Truly I tell you, all these things will happen before this generation has passed away. Heaven and earth will pass away; my words never will.

Keep watch, for the day is unknown

No one knows the day or the hour when that will come. The angels in heaven do not know it, and neither does the Son. Only the Father knows. The coming of the Son of Man will be like the days of Noah. Before the flood, people carried on with their meals and their drinking, with weddings for themselves and their children, right up to the day Noah went into the ark. They had no idea what was coming until the flood came and swept every one of them away. The coming of the Son of Man will be like that too. Two people will then be working in the field: one is taken, and the other is left. Two women will be grinding grain at the mill: one is taken, and the other is left. So stay alert, since you do not know which day your Lord will come. Think about this. A homeowner who knew at what time of night a thief was coming would stay awake and not allow anyone to dig through the walls of his house. So you too must stay prepared: the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not imagine.

The servant the master finds at work

Who, then, is the servant that is trustworthy and sensible, whom the master has put in charge of his household staff to give them their food when it is due? That servant will be blessed if, when his master comes, he finds him at that very work. Truly I tell you, the master will put him in charge of everything he owns. But that servant may be wicked. He may think to himself, ‘My master is a long time coming,’ and start to beat his fellow servants, while he eats and drinks with drunkards. If so, his master will come on a day he does not look for, at an hour he does not know. The master will cut him in pieces and put him with the hypocrites, where people will weep and grind their teeth.
fields.summary: Jesus foretells the temple’s destruction and speaks of the first birth pains, the call to flee to the mountains and the coming of the Son of Man on the clouds of heaven. No one knows the day, so the servants must keep watch.

fields.title: Matthew 25
fields.body_html:
Ten bridesmaids wait for the bridegroom

At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young women who were bridesmaids. They took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise. The foolish ones took their lamps but brought no oil along with them. But the wise ones took flasks of oil as well as their lamps. When the bridegroom was late in coming, every one of them nodded off and slept. In the middle of the night a shout was heard: ‘The bridegroom is here! Go out to meet him.’ Then all the young women woke up and got their lamps ready. The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Share some of your oil with us; our lamps are going out.’ But the wise ones replied, ‘We cannot; there would surely not be enough for both you and us. You had better go to the oil sellers and buy your own.’ While they were off buying it, the bridegroom arrived. The ones who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was closed. Later the rest of the young women came as well. ‘Lord, lord,’ they cried, ‘open the door for us!’ But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’ Keep awake, then, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

Servants entrusted with their master’s money

It is like a man about to travel abroad. He summoned his own servants and handed his property over to them. He gave five bags of silver to one, two to another and one to a third, according to what each could manage. Then he set off. At once the servant with the five bags went and did business with them and made five more. In the same way the one with two made two more. The servant who had received only one, however, went away and buried his master’s money in a hole in the ground. A long time afterward the master of those servants returned and went over the accounts with them. The one who had received five bags of silver came and brought five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you put five bags of silver in my care. See, I have made five more.’ His master answered, ‘Well done! You are a good and faithful servant. You proved faithful in small matters; I will put you in charge of great ones. Come in and share the joy of your master.’ The one with the two bags of silver came too. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you put two bags of silver in my care. See, I have made two more.’ His master answered, ‘Well done! You are a good and faithful servant. You proved faithful in small matters; I will put you in charge of great ones. Come in and share the joy of your master.’ Then the one who had received the one bag of silver came. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘I knew how hard a man you are. You reap fields you never sowed and gather grain where you scattered no seed. I was afraid, so I went off and buried your bag of silver in the ground. Here it is; you have what is yours.’ His master replied, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! So you knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter? In that case you should have handed my money to the bankers. On my return I would at least have got back what is mine, with interest. So take the bag of silver away from him and give it to the servant who has ten bags. For everyone who has will be given more, and they will have more than enough. But anyone who has nothing will lose even what they have. Throw this useless servant out into the darkness outside, where people will weep and grind their teeth.’

The Son of Man judges the nations

The Son of Man will come in his glory, and all the angels with him. Then he will take his seat on the throne of his glory. Every nation will be brought together before him. Then he will divide the people into two groups, the way a shepherd sorts the sheep from the goats. He will stand the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left. Then the King will say to those at his right, ‘Come, you whom my Father has blessed. The kingdom has been ready for you since the world was founded; now it is yours to inherit. For when I was hungry, you gave me food; when I was thirsty, you gave me a drink; when I was a stranger, you took me into your home; when I had no clothes, you dressed me; when I was sick, you looked after me; when I was in prison, you came to see me.’ Then the righteous will reply, ‘Lord, when was it that we saw you hungry and fed you, or thirsty and gave you a drink? When was it that we saw you a stranger and welcomed you in, or without clothes and dressed you? When was it that we saw you sick or in prison and came to you?’ The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, each time you did it for one of these my brothers and sisters, even the least of them, you did it for me.’ Then he will say to those at his left, ‘Go away from me, you who are under a curse, into the eternal fire that has been made ready for the devil and his angels. For when I was hungry, you gave me no food; when I was thirsty, you gave me nothing to drink; when I was a stranger, you did not take me into your home; when I had no clothes, you did not dress me; when I was sick and in prison, you did not look after me.’ Then they too will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, a stranger or without clothes, sick or in prison, and not come to your help?’ Then he will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, each time you failed to do it for one of these, even the least of them, you failed to do it for me.’ These will depart to eternal punishment, and the righteous will go to eternal life.”
fields.summary: Jesus tells of ten bridesmaids waiting for the bridegroom and of servants entrusted with their master’s money. The Son of Man will judge the nations, and what was done for the least of these was done for the king.

fields.title: Matthew 26
fields.body_html:
The plot against Jesus

When Jesus had finished all these words, he told his disciples, “As you know, the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

Then the chief priests and the elders of the people met in the courtyard of the high priest, a man named Caiaphas. There they made plans to arrest Jesus by some trick and put him to death. But they kept saying, “Not at the festival. We do not want the people to riot.”

A woman anoints Jesus at Bethany

While Jesus was at Bethany in the home of Simon, a man who had suffered from a skin disease, a woman came up to him with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfumed oil. As he sat at the table, she poured it over his head. Seeing this, the disciples were indignant. They said, “What is the point of such waste? It could have been sold for a large sum and the money given to the poor.” Jesus was aware of this and said to them, “Why make trouble for this woman? What she has done for me is a beautiful thing. The poor will always be among you, but I will not always be with you. By pouring this perfume over my body, she has made me ready to be buried. Truly I tell you, in every place in the whole world where this gospel is proclaimed, people will also tell what she has done, so that she is remembered.”

Then one of the Twelve, the man called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests and asked, “How much will you pay me to hand him over to you?” They paid him thirty silver coins. After that, Judas kept looking for the right moment to hand him over.

The Passover with the Twelve

On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where would you like us to get the Passover meal ready for you?” He told them, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My appointed time is near. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with my disciples.’” So the disciples followed Jesus’s instructions and got the Passover meal ready.

When evening came, Jesus took his place at the table with the twelve disciples. During the meal he said, “Truly I tell you, one of you is going to betray me.” They were deeply upset, and one after another they began to ask him, “Lord, it is not me, is it?” He replied, “Someone who has dipped his hand in the bowl along with me, he is the one who will betray me. The Son of Man goes on his way as the Scriptures have written of him, but woe to the one through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! Better for that man if he had never been born.” Then Judas, who was betraying him, said, “Rabbi, it is not me, is it?” Jesus told him, “You have said it yourself.”

During the meal Jesus took a loaf, said the blessing, and broke it. He gave it to the disciples and said, “Take it and eat. This is my body.” Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and passed it to them, saying, “Every one of you, drink from it. For this is my covenant blood, poured out for many to bring forgiveness of sins. But I tell you this: from now on I will not drink this fruit of the vine again until the day comes when I share it with you, new, in my Father’s kingdom.” Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.

Then Jesus told them, “This very night every one of you will fall away because of me. For it is written: ‘I will strike down the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will scatter in all directions.’ But after I have been raised, I will go to Galilee ahead of you.” Peter answered, “The others may all fall away because of you, but I will never fall away.” Jesus told him, “Truly I tell you, three times this very night you will deny me, before a rooster crows.” But Peter insisted, “I will never deny you, not even if it means dying with you!” Every one of the disciples said the same.

Jesus prays in Gethsemane

Jesus then came with them to a place named Gethsemane. He told the disciples, “Stay seated here while I go on over there and pray.” He took Peter and Zebedee’s two sons with him, and he began to be filled with grief and anguish. Then he said to them, “My soul is weighed down with grief, even to death. Stay here and keep awake with me.” He went a little farther, threw himself face down on the ground, and prayed, “My Father, if there is any way, let this cup pass by me. But not what I want; what you want.” Then he came back to the disciples and found them asleep. He said to Peter, “So none of you could stay awake with me for even one hour? Stay alert and pray that you will not come into testing. The spirit is eager, but human nature is weak.” He went away again, a second time, and prayed: “My Father, if there is no way for this to pass unless I drink it, then let your will be done.” When he came back, he again found them asleep; they could not keep their eyes open. So he left them, went away once more, and prayed a third time, saying the same words. Then he came to the disciples and said to them, “Go on sleeping, then, and resting. The hour is here: the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners. Get up; let us be going. Here comes the man who is betraying me.”

Judas’s kiss and the arrest

Jesus had not finished speaking when Judas, one of the Twelve, came up. A large crowd came with him, carrying swords and clubs. The chief priests and the elders of the people had sent them. The betrayer had given them a sign: “The man I kiss is the one you want. Arrest him.” Judas went straight to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” Then he kissed him. Jesus said to him, “Friend, get on with what you are here for.” At that, the crowd moved in. They laid hands on Jesus and arrested him. One of the men with Jesus reached for his sword and drew it. He struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his ear. Then Jesus told him, “Put your sword back where it belongs. Everyone who takes up the sword will die by the sword. Do you not know that I could ask my Father, and he would send me more than twelve legions of angels right away? But if I did, how could the Scriptures come true? They say that all this has to take place.” Then Jesus said to the crowd, “Am I some bandit, that you come out with swords and clubs to seize me? Day after day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest me then.” All this took place so that what the prophets wrote in the Scriptures would come true. At that, every one of the disciples abandoned him and ran off.

Jesus before the council

The men who had arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas the high priest. The scribes and the elders had gathered there. Peter kept him in sight from far behind and came as far as the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and took a seat among the guards, waiting to see what the end would be. Meanwhile the chief priests and the whole council were trying to find false charges against Jesus that would get him executed. Many false witnesses came forward, yet they found none. At last two of them stepped up and stated, “This man claimed, ‘I am able to tear down the temple of God and build it again within three days.’” Then the high priest stood up and said to him, “Have you no answer? What about the evidence these men are bringing against you?” Jesus, however, said nothing. Then the high priest said to him, “In the name of the living God I place you under oath. Tell us: are you the Christ, the Son of God?” Jesus answered him, “You have said it yourself. Yet this I tell you all: from this time on, you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power, and coming on the clouds of heaven.” The high priest then ripped his robes and cried, “This is blasphemy! What use do we have for more witnesses? You have now heard the blasphemy yourselves. What is your verdict?” They answered, “He deserves to die.” Next they spat in his face and pounded him with their fists, while others struck him with open hands and jeered, “Prophesy for us, Christ! Which one of us hit you?” Meanwhile Peter was sitting out in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, “You were with Jesus the Galilean too.” But Peter denied it with everyone listening. “I have no idea what you mean,” he said. He went out toward the gateway, where another servant girl saw him and told the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth.” Again he denied it, this time with an oath: “I do not know the man!” Before long the people standing nearby came up to Peter. “You are certainly one of them,” they said. “The way you talk betrays you.” Then he began cursing and swearing, “I do not know the man!” At that very moment a rooster crowed. Then Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” And he went outside and broke down in bitter tears.
fields.summary: The leaders plot against Jesus, a woman anoints Jesus at Bethany, and Judas agrees to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver. At the Passover with the Twelve Jesus gives the bread and the cup, prays in Gethsemane, and is arrested and condemned by the council, while Peter denies Jesus three times.

fields.title: Matthew 27
fields.body_html:
Jesus handed over to Pilate

Early in the morning all the chief priests and the elders of the people met and reached their decision against Jesus: he must be put to death. They tied him up, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate, the governor.

Judas and the thirty pieces of silver

When Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that Jesus had been condemned, he was seized with regret and took the thirty silver coins back to the chief priests and the elders. “I have sinned,” he said. “I have handed an innocent man over to death.” They answered, “Why should that concern us? That is your affair.” Judas flung the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself. The chief priests gathered up the coins. “The law does not let us put this into the temple treasury,” they said, “because it was paid to bring about a death.” They talked it over and decided to buy the Potter’s Field with the money, as a place to bury people from other lands. This is why that field has had the name Field of Blood ever since, up to the present day. Then the word spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled: “They took the thirty silver coins, the price set on the one whose value some of the people of Israel had fixed, and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord had instructed me.”

Jesus before the governor

Jesus now stood in front of the governor, who questioned him: “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus replied, “It is you who say it.” But when the chief priests and the elders brought their charges against him, he made no reply. Then Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear all the charges they are bringing against you?” Still Jesus did not answer him on even one point, and the governor was deeply amazed at this.

At each festival the governor used to set free one prisoner for the crowd, whichever one they wanted. At that time they were holding a prisoner everyone knew of, called Jesus Barabbas. When the crowd had gathered, Pilate asked them, “Which one do you want me to set free for you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?” He was aware that envy had moved them to hand Jesus over.

As Pilate sat on the judgment seat, a message came to him from his wife: “Leave that righteous man alone. Today in a dream I went through great distress over him.”

But the chief priests and the elders talked the crowds into asking for Barabbas and having Jesus put to death. The governor asked them again, “Which of these two do you want me to set free for you?” “Barabbas!” they said. Pilate asked them, “Then what am I to do with Jesus who is called Christ?” They all shouted, “Let him be crucified!” “But what wrong has he done?” Pilate asked. But they only shouted louder and louder, “Let him be crucified!” Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere and that an uproar was starting instead. So he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. “I am not guilty of this man’s death,” he said. “That is your affair.” All the people there answered, “Let the guilt for his death fall on us and on our children!” So Pilate let Barabbas go free, as they wanted. As for Jesus, Pilate ordered him to be scourged, and then handed him over for crucifixion.

The soldiers mock the King of the Jews

The governor’s soldiers then brought Jesus inside the governor’s headquarters, and the entire cohort assembled around him. They took off his clothes and put a scarlet military cloak on him. They twisted thorny branches into a crown and set it on his head, and put a stick in his right hand. Then they went down on their knees in front of him and made fun of him: “Hail, King of the Jews!” They spat on him, and took the stick and beat him over the head with it again and again. After they had finished mocking him, they stripped off the cloak and dressed him again in his own clothes. Then they led him out to be crucified.

Jesus is crucified

On their way out they came across a man from Cyrene named Simon, and they forced him to carry Jesus’s cross.

They arrived at a place named Golgotha, a name meaning Place of a Skull. They gave him wine to drink that had gall mixed into it. He tasted it but would not drink it. When they had crucified him, they shared out his clothes among themselves by drawing lots. Then they sat down there and kept guard over him. Over his head they placed the charge against him in writing: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”

Two bandits were crucified along with him, one at his right and the other at his left. People going past heaped insults on him and shook their heads. “So you were going to tear down the temple and build it again in three days!” they said. “Save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!” In the same way the chief priests made fun of him, along with the scribes and the elders. They said, “He saved others, yet he has no power to save himself. The King of Israel, is he? Then let him come down off the cross this moment, and we will believe in him. He put his trust in God, so let God rescue him now, if God really wants him. For he said, ‘I am God’s Son.’” Even the bandits crucified alongside him heaped the same insults on him.

The death of Jesus

At noon darkness fell over the whole land, and it lasted until three in the afternoon. At about three o’clock Jesus gave a loud cry: “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” That means, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?” Hearing it, some of those who stood nearby said, “This fellow is calling for Elijah!” At once one of them ran and got a sponge. He soaked it in sour wine, put it on the end of a stick, and held it up for him to drink. But the rest told him, “Wait, let us see whether Elijah will come to save him.” Once more Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and he yielded up his spirit. Then the temple curtain split in two, from the top all the way to the bottom. The ground shook and rocks were torn apart. Graves were opened, and the bodies of many of God’s holy people who had fallen asleep in death were raised. Coming out of the graves after Jesus was raised, they went into the holy city and showed themselves to many people.

The centurion and the men with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and everything that was happening, and they were filled with fear. “This man truly was God’s Son!” they said.

A number of women stood watching from far off. These women had come with Jesus all the way from Galilee, providing for him. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.

The burial and the guard at the tomb

As evening came on, Joseph arrived, a rich man from the town of Arimathea who had also become one of Jesus’s disciples. He went to Pilate and requested Jesus’s body. Pilate then ordered that it be handed over to him. Joseph took the body and wound a clean linen sheet around it. Then he placed it in the new tomb he had carved in the rock for himself, rolled a great stone across the doorway of the tomb, and went away. Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary too, seated facing the tomb.

On the following day, the one after the day of Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees came together to Pilate. “Sir,” they said, “we have remembered something that impostor said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will be raised.’ Give the command, then, to have the tomb guarded securely until the third day. If not, his disciples could come, take him away by stealth, and announce to the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead.’ And this final fraud would do more harm than the first one.” Pilate told them, “You may have a guard. Go and secure it in whatever way you think best.” They went and sealed the stone, and with the guard in place they made the tomb secure.
fields.summary: Jesus is handed over to Pilate, and Judas, seized with remorse, hangs himself. The crowd chooses Barabbas, the soldiers mock Jesus as King of the Jews, and Jesus is crucified and dies; Joseph of Arimathea buries the body and a guard is set at the tomb.

fields.title: Matthew 28
fields.body_html:
The tomb is empty

The Sabbath was over, and the first day of the week was just beginning to dawn, when Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the tomb. Suddenly the earth shook violently, because an angel of the Lord had come down from heaven. He went to the stone, rolled it back and sat on it. He looked like a flash of lightning, and his clothing was snow-white. In terror of him the guards trembled, and they became like dead men. But the angel said to the women, “You need not be afraid. I know that you are looking for Jesus, the one who was crucified. He is not here. He has been raised, just as he foretold. Come and see where he was lying. Hurry now, and give his disciples this message: ‘He has been raised from the dead! He is on his way to Galilee ahead of you, and that is where you will see him.’ That is my message to you.” Quickly the women left the tomb. Fear and great joy filled them as they ran to tell his disciples. All at once Jesus stood in their path. “Greetings!” he said to them. They went to him, held on to his feet and bowed in worship before him. Then Jesus told them, “Have no fear. Go and take word to my brothers: they are to set out for Galilee, and there they will see me.”

The guards’ story

The women were still on their way when some of the soldiers from the guard came into the city and gave the chief priests a full report of what had happened. After meeting with the elders and deciding what to do, the chief priests paid the soldiers a large sum of money and gave them their story: “Tell people, ‘His disciples came in the night while we were asleep and stole him away.’ If the governor hears about this, we will win him over and see that you have nothing to worry about.” The soldiers took the money and followed their instructions.

And this is the account that has gone around among Jews up to the present day.

Sent to all the nations

The eleven disciples made their way to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had appointed for them. When they saw him there, they bowed in worship, but some had doubts. Jesus came up to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been placed in my hands. Go, then, and make disciples of all the nations: baptize them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teach them to keep everything I have commanded you. And remember this: I myself am with you every day, until the close of the age.”
fields.summary: At dawn the women find the tomb empty and meet the risen Jesus, while the guards are paid to spread a false story. On a mountain in Galilee Jesus sends the eleven disciples to make disciples of all the nations.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
Jesus came up to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been placed in my hands. Go, then, and make disciples of all the nations: baptize them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teach them to keep everything I have commanded you. And remember this: I myself am with you every day, until the close of the age.”

— Matthew 28:18–20

Matthew ends where Jesus began his teaching, on a mountain in Galilee. There is no ascension scene, no farewell, not even an “Amen”. The last word is a promise, and the book stops while it is still sounding. The Gospel that began with a family line reaching back to Abraham closes with a family about to reach out to every nation on earth.

The question the book leaves with you

At the turning point of the Gospel, Jesus asks his disciples two questions. The first is easy: who do people say the Son of Man is? Some say John the Baptist, some Elijah, some Jeremiah or another prophet. The second is not:

Then he asked them, “And you, who do you say that I am?”

— Matthew 16:15

Matthew has been answering that question since his first verse. Jesus is the son of David and the son of Abraham; Immanuel, God with us; the one who will save his people from their sins; the teacher with authority of his own; the Son in whom the Father delights; the king of the Jews on a Roman cross. But the question is put to the disciples, not to the crowds, and the book puts it to its readers in the same way. It is not enough to know what others say.

And the answer is meant to be lived. The Sermon on the Mount ends with a storm and two houses. In Matthew’s great picture of the judgment, the King says to those on his right that whatever they did for the least of his brothers and sisters, “you did it for me.” Neither the sheep nor the goats knew whom they were serving or neglecting. Matthew’s Jesus cares about what we confess and about what we do, and he will not let us have the one without the other.

Where the book points

It points, first, to the nations. The command to “make disciples of all the nations” has sent the church to the ends of the earth, and the book shows what that means. Disciples are made by baptism into the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and by teaching people to keep everything Jesus commanded, the commands this Gospel has so carefully gathered into its five great sermons.

It points, second, to the church: a community gathered in Jesus’s name, where two or three are enough for him to be among them, and where forgiveness has no ceiling.

And it points to the end. Matthew’s Jesus speaks often of the close of the age, of a harvest, a wedding feast, a master returning from a journey. He also says plainly that no one knows the day or the hour, not the angels, not even the Son. The right response is not to calculate but to be ready, and to be found faithful.

Where to go from here

Matthew has been preached and expounded more than almost any book of the Bible, and some of its best interpreters are in this library. A few places to begin:

  • Through the whole Gospel. John Chrysostom’s Homilies on Matthew, ninety sermons preached at Antioch, the fullest commentary from the early church; and J. C. Ryle’s Expository Thoughts on Matthew, plain and warm, chapter by chapter.
  • On the Sermon on the Mount (5–7). Thomas Watson’s The Beatitudes (5:3–12) and his The Lord’s Prayer (6:9–13); Alexander Maclaren’s The First Beatitude (5:3); and three sermons by Martyn Lloyd-Jones, The Salt of the Earth (5:13), The Light of the World (5:14–16) and God or Mammon (6:19–24).
  • On Jesus’s invitation (11:28–30). Maclaren’s The Rest Giver and John Newton’s Messiah’s Easy Yoke.
  • On weak faith. Charles H. Spurgeon’s Sweet Comfort for Feeble Saints, on the bent reed and the wick that is barely burning (12:20), and Augustine of Hippo’s Peter on the Waves (14:25–31).
  • On Peter’s confession (16:17). Jonathan Edwards’s A Divine and Supernatural Light, on what it means that “No human being showed you this”.
  • On the resurrection (28:6). Christmas Evans’s The Resurrection of Jesus.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to Matthew in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this Gospel.

But the best next step may be to read Matthew again, with the end in view. Knowing how it finishes, you will notice how often the nations were already at the door: the magi, the centurion, the Canaanite woman, the soldiers at the cross. You will notice how often Jesus promised to be present. And you may hear the last words of the book as they were meant, not as a farewell, but as a promise for every day of your own life:

“I myself am with you every day, until the close of the age.”

— Matthew 28:20
